message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Best direct match to the target trait (alcohol dependence) is the score explicitly built and evaluated for alcohol use disorder/alcohol dependence (trait_efo: alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported: Alcohol use disorder). Compared with PGS000201/PGS000202 (problematic alcohol use; DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed), PGS002738 is closer to a disease endpoint rather than a quantitative/problem-use construct. Performance reporting is limited across all candidates (no PRS-only AUC/R2), so selection leans on endpoint fidelity plus the available effect-size evidence: PGS002738 reports a reasonably strong stratification metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900), which is more compelling than the smaller incremental ΔR² values reported for PGS000201/PGS000202. PGS002739 is AUD-focused but evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples, making it less generally applicable when deployment ancestry is unspecified; thus PGS002738 is the strongest overall direct candidate in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004913","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct concept matches to alcoholic liver cirrhosis, so endpoint fidelity does not separate them strongly. The main differentiator is how interpretable the reported performance is as PRS-driven (vs covariate-driven) and whether the score is a genuine polygenic model.

- PGS000704 is a large, framework-style UKB score with only a full-model C-index (0.711) reported under a time-to-event setup with covariates; it does not provide PRS-only discrimination, and its biomarker-focused publication context makes it less clearly disease-optimized for alcoholic cirrhosis.
- PGS001777 is essentially a 3-variant genetic risk score with unknown covariates and a small validation sample (n=1,390); despite an AUROC reported, it is not a robust polygenic predictor.
- PGS004913 is a recent disease-focused PRS for alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, uses a standard PRS pipeline (PRSice-2), reports PRS-attributable signal (R²=0.029; OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4), and uses basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Even though its training/validation sizes are modest, its evidence package is the most directly PRS-informative among the candidates.

Because none of the candidates report clean PRS-only AUROC and the available metrics are not perfectly comparable, the selection is direct but not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are for ankylosing spondylitis, but PGS001267 is the cleanest direct-match endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Ankylosing spondylitis) with explicit PRS-only performance reported in a large European validation (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.7265; PGS R² no covariates 0.0988; n=67,425) and only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). PGS001268 has slightly higher metrics but is a time-to-event phenotype (TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic disease-risk target. Other options either lack PRS-comparable AUC/R² (PGS001876/PGS002089) or have small East Asian-only validation with only full-model AUROC and unknown covariates (PGS003420–PGS003424), making them less comparable for general selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS005252 is the only candidate with exact endpoint alignment to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported = incident aortic stenosis cases), whereas the other candidates are for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or aortic valve function measurements. It is a modern genome-wide method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (~1.1M) and large European evaluation sample (n=446,895), supporting robustness in the stated ancestry context. Although the reported discrimination is a full-model C-index (0.87) with multiple clinical covariates (so not directly comparable as PRS-only performance), it still provides supportive evidence within an otherwise best-matched, disease-focused aortic stenosis score family; competing aortic stenosis scores (PGS005254-005256) lack comparable discrimination metrics and show weaker effect-size evidence (HR 1.53–1.64 vs 1.92 for PGS005252)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Best direct match to the target trait \"arthritis\" is the score explicitly built and evaluated for the same broad endpoint: PGS001135 (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported=\"Arthritis (nos)\"). It also reports PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.539; PGS R2 no covariates=0.00291) and incremental AUROC (0.00314), which—while modest—are more comparable and informative for PRS quality than the many candidates that only report full-model AUROC or effect sizes under different arthritis subtypes (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, gout, osteoarthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis). Other arthritis-labeled candidates (PGS004477/PGS004547) lack comparable discrimination metrics and provide only an OR without clear PRS-only context, making them less informative despite being label-matched. Overall, PGS001135 is a direct endpoint match but sub-optimal in absolute PRS signal strength."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"High","rationale":"PGS001344 is the strongest direct-match asthma score in this fixed list based on (1) endpoint fidelity and (2) availability of PRS-comparable performance evidence in a large European validation.

- Endpoint/phenotype: “Asthma (diagnosed by doctor)” is a clean, direct asthma diagnosis endpoint (good match for generic asthma).
- Performance evidence quality: Unlike many candidates that report only full-model AUROC (often covariate-influenced) or only effect sizes, PGS001344 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates = 0.64568; PGS R2 no covariates = 0.05973) plus full-model AUROC 0.66621 with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). This makes it more comparable and informative for ranking.
- Validation context: Large European validation sample (n=19,857) and consistent reporting (CIs provided) support robustness.

Other candidates either have weaker/less comparable endpoints (e.g., pediatric/childhood-only, onset/time-to-event variants), smaller validation, heavier non-genetic risk-score covariates, or lack PRS-only metrics; some have large N but only incremental/full-model R2 without isolating PRS contribution. Therefore PGS001344 is the best overall choice for the target trait asthma."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Best direct-match for target trait atopic eczema/atopic dermatitis with the strongest structural PRS construction among candidates: PRS-CS genome-wide model (~1.09M variants) evaluated in a large European sample (n=337,910) on an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint. Competing candidates either (a) focus on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients (endpoint mismatch despite reported AUROCs/ORs), or (b) report only full-model AUROC/R² with covariates and small validation (PGS001773) making the very high AUROC likely non-PRS-comparable. PGS004587 has a similar incident endpoint and validation size but is a much smaller genome-wide-significant SNP set (23 variants), so is structurally less likely to capture polygenic signal than PRS-CS."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS005168 is the strongest direct-match candidate for atrial fibrillation in this fixed list based on endpoint fidelity plus the overall evidence package. It targets atrial fibrillation with matching EFO and phenotyping_reported (direct AF, not a proxy or fixed-horizon risk wrapper), and it comes from a large, disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis context (many contributing cohorts listed) rather than a single-biobank portability/framework exercise. Its selected European validation reports a high full-model C-index (0.8718) with a clearly stated covariate set that includes basic demographics/technical factors plus CHARGE-AF; while this is not a PRS-only metric (so it cannot be compared as pure PRS discrimination), it is still supportive when combined with the strong study design and direct endpoint alignment. Competing models either (i) have weaker/older evidence with smaller or less informative validation, (ii) focus on AF+flutter or time-to-event variants without clearly stronger PRS-only metrics, or (iii) report high full-model C-index values in settings where PRS-only performance is not isolated. Given these tradeoffs, PGS005168 is the best-supported, disease-focused AF score among the candidates, though confidence is moderated because PRS-only AUROC/R2 is not provided here."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS001263 is the only candidate with an exact endpoint match to the target trait across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (atrial flutter), whereas the other candidates are for the broader combined phenotype atrial fibrillation and flutter (including a time-to-event definition for PGS001339). It also reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates = 0.617 and PGS R² no covariates = 0.025), making it directly comparable as a standalone genetic score; the higher full-model AUROC is largely covariate-driven and not used as the primary ranking signal. Given similar UKB EUR development context across candidates and the lack of PRS-only AUC/R² for the portability-paper scores (PGS001841/PGS002050), the clean trait match plus available PRS-only metrics makes PGS001263 the best choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000327 is the best direct match for autism spectrum disorder because its endpoint fidelity is clean across all three label fields (trait_reported, trait_efo, and phenotyping_reported all specify autism spectrum disorder), whereas PGS002790 has a clear endpoint mismatch (phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite sharing the ASD label fields. In addition, PGS000327 comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS/consortium context (Nat Genet; multiple ASD cohorts listed), which is a stronger study archetype signal than the more cross-trait/behavioral framing of PGS002790. Although neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R², PGS000327 provides supportive effect-size evidence (OR per SD ~1.33) and a higher reported R² metric than PGS002790 (noting these appear to be full-model/partial metrics and thus are only weakly comparable). Both are EUR-evaluated, so ancestry does not differentiate. Overall, the decisive factor is endpoint fidelity plus disease-focused development, favoring PGS000327."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000119","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are broadly on-target for basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo, but most provide only full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUC/R2), so small AUROC differences are not reliably comparable across records. Among the direct BCC endpoints with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch), PGS000119 shows the strongest reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.64, 95% CI 0.62–0.66) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.56–1.75), with a larger validation sample (n=20,468) than the closely competing PRSweb/Cancer PRSweb scores. Newer 2023/2025 scores (PGS003416/PGS003417/PGS005207) lack discrimination metrics here and/or have less generic phenotyping (keratinocyte cancers; childhood cancer survivors), so they are less compelling for general BCC risk prediction given this candidate set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001824","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are broadly aligned to the target EFO concept (bilirubin metabolism disease). However, PGS000924 uses a time-to-event composite endpoint (“disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”), which is a weaker endpoint match than a direct bilirubin disorder diagnosis, and its extremely high AUROC/R² come from a high-throughput UKB framework context where such outlier performance can be less reliable/comparable. Between the two direct-match models (PGS001824 and PGS002032), they share the same endpoint, publication, training cohort, covariates, and identical reported validation metric (partial-r=0.0716), so performance evidence does not differentiate them. In that tie, the simpler penalized-regression score with far fewer variants (PGS001824; 22 variants) is preferred as a more parsimonious, easier-to-deploy model without sacrificing reported validation performance versus the 19,768-variant LDpred2 alternative."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are SDPR scores trained on PGC EUR GWAS and evaluated in EUR, so method and ancestry transportability do not differentiate them. The main differentiator is endpoint fidelity: despite having trait_reported/trait_efo aligned to bipolar disorder subtypes, each record’s phenotyping_reported is not a bipolar disorder diagnosis endpoint (it references cognition/behavior traits), making the set overall a weak match for deploying a bipolar disorder risk PGS. Given that limitation, PGS002786 is the least subtype-restricted (bipolar disorder rather than bipolar I/II) and therefore the closest semantic match to the target trait; its reported partial R² is similar in magnitude to the others, so choosing the broadest label is the most defensible tie-break. Confidence is low because none provides PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/R²) on a bipolar disorder case-control endpoint."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS001033 is the only candidate whose trait_efo directly matches the target umbrella trait (“blood coagulation disease”), whereas PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency subtype (different EFO). It also provides directly PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC and PGS-only R² reported) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), and has substantially larger validation size (n=67,425) than the congenital-deficiency scores (n=19,864) which report only partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R². Although its phenotyping is time-to-event (a mild endpoint-design warning), the overall endpoint alignment plus availability of PRS-only metrics makes it the strongest direct-match option in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS004153 is the strongest direct match for the target trait (trait_efo = breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported = Breast cancer) among the provided candidates, with a modern genome-wide method (MultiPRS ensemble) and the best reported discrimination in a large European validation (full-model AUROC 0.6625; R² 0.0764) while using no additional covariates (covariates = 0), making the performance signal more PRS-comparable than many alternatives whose AUROC is likely boosted by clinical covariates (e.g., family history, risk models). It also outperforms other high-performing breast-cancer candidates in the list (e.g., LDpred2-auto/CV around AUROC ~0.6598) and avoids endpoint mismatches (subtype-only, BRCA-carrier-only, survival/aggressiveness endpoints). Confidence is Moderate because many records report only full-model metrics and cross-study metric comparability is imperfect, but within the same evaluation framework cluster PGS004153 has the best overall evidence package."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001301","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS001301 is the strongest direct-match candidate because it provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates = 0.82867; PGS R² no covariates = 0.14224) with clearly stated basic covariates for the full model (age, sex, array, PCs), enabling more comparable assessment than candidates that report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for the target (trait_efo is celiac disease; phenotyping is a combined malabsorption/coeliac disease label that still explicitly includes coeliac disease). Competing models either (a) are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (PGS000041/PGS000042), making them less general for overall celiac disease risk, or (b) report only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics (PGS000040/PGS000316/PGS004930), which is less reliable for ranking PRS quality. Portability-framework scores (PGS001856/PGS002067 etc.) provide only partial-correlation metrics here, which are harder to compare directly to AUROC/R² and do not outweigh the clear PRS-only metrics available for PGS001301."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001299","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches to the target concept (trait_efo cervical carcinoma; phenotyping is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer), so endpoint fidelity does not separate them. The key differentiator is availability of PRS-comparable performance: PGS001299 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.552 and PGS R2 no covariates 0.00263) plus incremental AUROC, which isolates the PRS contribution; the other candidates mainly report full-model AUROC/C-index with substantial non-genetic covariates (e.g., parity, oral contraceptive use, smoking) or without PRS-only metrics, making cross-model ranking by their higher full-model AUC unreliable. Although PGS001299’s PRS-only discrimination is modest, it is the most interpretable and comparable evidence package in this fixed list, with clean basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and explicit separation of PRS-only vs full-model performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004546","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Best direct-match choice for cholelithiasis is PGS004546. Endpoint fidelity is strong (ICD K80 cholelithiasis; trait_efo matches), and it comes from a disease-focused prediction paper rather than a pan-trait/portability framework (which are systematically weaker generalizers). Although it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R², it reports an OR per SD of ~1.30, indicating moderate discriminative signal; within the same publication family it also improves on the companion LDpred2 disease-only score (PGS004476 OR ~1.22), consistent with the intended metaPRS integration. Alternatives are less attractive: PGS001174 is a sparse pan-trait UKB framework score despite having PRS-only AUROC/R²; PGS001861/PGS002072 are UKB portability-framework scores with only partial-r; PGS005150 is evaluated only in East Asian samples, making it less generally applicable when deployment ancestry is unspecified."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS002237 is the strongest direct-match candidate in this fixed list because it comes from a CKD-focused, disease-specific study (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”, Nat Med 2022) with a clinically clear CKD definition (stage ≥3 / eGFR <45) and multi-ancestry evaluation. Many other candidates either (a) lack comparable performance evidence and/or have endpoint mismatches (e.g., PGS000728 uses eGFR as a quantitative proxy; PGS000859 is tied to a diabetes subtype phenotype; PGS004224 is a secondhand-smoke interaction framing), or (b) are pan-trait/framework-style (PGS001272) with explicitly weak PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.536; PGS-only R² ~0.002). Although PGS002237 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.78) with heavy clinical covariates (so the AUROC is not directly interpretable as PRS-only performance), its endpoint fidelity and disease-focused development/validation package make it the best overall choice among the available options."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Best direct match for the target trait (COPD) with a disease-focused, multi-biobank GWAS training context and a substantially stronger PRS-comparable metric than the UKB sparse snpnet COPD variants: it reports Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out (0.0381), which is the most informative PRS-only-style performance evidence in this candidate set. Competing COPD snpnet models (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334) have much lower PGS-only R2 (~0.002–0.003) and small incremental AUROC, suggesting limited standalone PRS signal despite similar full-model AUROC. Other candidates either target a related but not identical phenotype (emphysema; chronic airway obstruction) or lack comparable PRS-only metrics (only ORs with unknown covariates), reducing confidence for ranking them above PGS001783."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is broad “cirrhosis of liver”. Among candidates with exact trait_efo alignment (PGS000726, PGS000776, PGS004621), PGS004621 has the strongest overall evidence package: (1) endpoint fidelity is direct (“Cirrhosis” with phenotyping_reported “Cirrhosis”), matching the target without restricting to alcohol-only subtypes; (2) modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), a strong structural signal versus genome-wide-significant-only scores (12 variants in PGS000726; 9 variants in PGS000776); (3) large multi-cohort training/validation context with very large reported validation sample size (n=1,153,995) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), reducing concerns about covariate-inflated performance; (4) reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.68) is comparable to other cirrhosis candidates, but given lack of PGS-only AUC/R2 across the pool, method family + endpoint match are more reliable differentiators than small full-model AUROC differences. Alcohol-specific models (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) are less direct matches to the broad target cirrhosis endpoint."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches: trait_efo exactly matches the target and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported are the same congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint. Both come from the same UKB portability paper, with the same training N (391,124), validation ancestry (European selected), validation N (19,864), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and essentially identical reported partial correlation (~0.056). With performance effectively tied, structural signals dominate: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 and includes far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally a stronger polygenic modeling choice than a very sparse penalized-regression score when endpoints and evaluation context are otherwise identical."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Both candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_reported/EFO/phenotyping all corneal dystrophy) and come from the same UK Biobank portability framework with the same training N, covariates, validation ancestry context, and the same type of reported metric (partial correlation). With endpoint and study context essentially tied, the main differentiator is structural: PGS002042 uses an LDpred2 genome-wide approach with 59,944 variants versus PGS001835’s penalized regression model with only 38 variants. Within this same-publication, same-endpoint setting, the much higher variant count is a meaningful signal of capturing more polygenic signal, and PGS002042 also shows a slightly higher partial-r (0.0471 vs 0.0384) in the selected European validation record. Therefore PGS002042 is the best available candidate, though confidence is moderated because neither model reports PRS-only AUC/R²."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000013 is a direct match to the target (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both coronary artery disease) and, among the candidates, it provides the clearest PRS-comparable performance evidence: an explicit PGS-only R² (0.04) alongside a large European validation sample (n=288,978). Many alternatives report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with heavier or unclear covariate packaging) or only effect sizes without PRS-only metrics, making cross-model comparison less reliable. While some candidates show higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000018, PGS001780), those are not PRS-only metrics and may be substantially covariate-driven; PGS000013’s explicit PGS-only R² makes it the most interpretable high-quality choice for generic CAD genetic risk prediction in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001331","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo, but PGS001330 uses a time-to-event phenotype (weaker endpoint fidelity for generic disease risk) while PGS001331 uses a straightforward Crohn’s disease phenotype. Between the two UKB snpnet scores, PGS001331 has slightly better PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621) with similar basic covariates and the same European validation size (n=24,905), making it the stronger of the pair.\n\nPGS004254 reports a much higher AUROC (0.72) but only as a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R² shown), so it is not reliably comparable for ranking PRS quality; its smaller training sample (n=12,331) also provides less reassurance than the UKB framework scores. The selected PGS-only R² for PGS001331 is far below Crohn’s disease heritability estimates, so it is plausible and not suggestive of metric inflation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000929","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is dementia. Among candidates, PGS000929 is the cleanest direct match on trait_efo (dementia) with a broadly relevant endpoint (algorithmically-defined all-cause dementia) rather than Alzheimer’s-disease-only or restricted subgroups. It also reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.627 and PGS-only R²=0.02346) plus incremental AUROC, enabling more reliable assessment of the genetic score’s standalone contribution than most dementia-labeled alternatives that report only HR/partial-r or full-model-only metrics. Competing dementia EFO scores include PGS000946 (unspecified dementia TTE) with lower PGS-only AUROC/R², and PGS005170 (incident all-cause dementia) but with only full-model AUROC reported and small development/validation N, making PRS-only strength harder to judge. Therefore PGS000929 is the best-supported direct dementia PGS in this fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002036","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Best direct match to target trait “depressive disorder” with coherent endpoint alignment (trait_efo: depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported: Depression) and a strong modern genome-wide method (LDpred2) with high variant count (807,338), which is a favorable structural signal when PRS-only AUC/R² are not reported across most candidates. Competing models either (a) use weaker proxy/minimal-phenotyping endpoints (e.g., GP/psychiatrist visit proxies), (b) have endpoint mismatch to non-depression outcomes (e.g., antidepressant side effects, brain imaging traits), (c) are very sparse GWS SNP scores, or (d) report only full-model metrics that are not PRS-comparable. PGS002036 also comes from a portability-focused study with multi-ancestry evaluation, supporting broader transportability context even though the selected validation ancestry here is European."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004862","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy at the EFO level and use a strong genome-wide method (PRS-CS). The cleanest endpoint match for the target trait is the pair with phenotyping_reported = \"Dilated cardiomyopathy\" and EUR GWAS/EUR evaluation (PGS004861/PGS004862). Between those two, the MTAG-enhanced version is mildly preferred per endpoint-label guidance and also has slightly better reported discrimination/effect size in the same validation context (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; OR per SD 1.76 vs 1.56) with comparable basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs). Other 2024-12-16 scores report explicit PRS-only AUCs but are evaluated in MAE-only or have phenotype shifts to \"Non-ischemic\" or \"Clinical\" DCM with less straightforward alignment to the generic target label, so they are not preferred over the direct DCM EUR-evaluated MTAG score. Confidence is Moderate because the leading candidates report only full-model AUROC/R² (no explicit PRS-only AUC/R²), limiting strict PRS-only comparability."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000997","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000997 is the best direct match for the target trait (diverticular disease): it targets diverticular disease of intestine with EFO diverticular disease, and—unlike the 2024 candidates—reports clear PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 and PGS-only R² 0.0178) in European validation. It also shows a larger incremental AUROC (0.0173) than PGS000996 (0.0084), indicating stronger standalone PRS contribution. PGS000996 is a close alternative but has materially weaker PRS-only metrics (AUROC 0.552; R² 0.0037). The newer PGS004474/PGS004544 provide only per-SD ORs (~1.31–1.32) with unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics, and PGS004614 reports only a covariate-augmented full-model AUROC (includes family history) without PGS-only metrics and with small validation N, making it less comparable for ranking PRS quality. Confidence is moderate because the strongest disease-focused 2024 scores lack PRS-only AUC/R² in the visible record, limiting direct comparability."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001254","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct endpoint matches for Dupuytren contracture (phenotyping_reported aligns closely across records). PGS001254 is the only candidate with explicit PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6646; PGS-only R²=0.0247), allowing a more reliable assessment of standalone PRS signal than the portability-study scores that report only partial correlation. Although PGS001880/PGS002092 have larger training N and many more variants, their reported metric (partial-r) is less directly comparable to AUROC/R² for deployment-style PRS evaluation, and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided. Given comparable covariate sets (basic demographics + PCs) and direct phenotype match, the availability of clear PRS-only performance evidence makes PGS001254 the best-supported choice."}
